newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey to boost animal husbandry, eyes exports.
newsitem.headline: Turkey to boost animal husbandry, eyes exports.

text.p: Turkey will give incentives worth a total $220 million to animal breeders in its poor eastern region, Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said on Wednesday.
He also said Turkey would become a net meat exporter after the incentives.

"We will give as incentives 12 trillion lira for animal breeding and 12 trillion lira for species rehabilitation projects," he told reporters before a cabinet meeting held at the eastern town of Agri, a key centre for animal husbandry.
He said Turkey's meat production would rise by 100,000 tonnes from the current 943,000 tonnes after incentives were fully in place.
"The number of animals for breeding can be raised up to 2.5 million from 1.13 million now," he said.
Turkey numbers about 11.8 million livestock and imports about 58,000 tonnes of meat annually.
"We will come to a position of exporting about 50,000 tonnes of meat," Erbakan said.

The cabinet met in Agri for its weekly meeting to unveil other measures of government support for the economically backward eastern and southeastern regions, where the population is predominantly Kurdish.
